run_metadata.coverage_summary: Network constraint unchanged from the 2026-10-05 onward runs: every direct WebFetch again failed at the egress proxy with DNS errors (ENOTFOUND), confirmed against example.com as well as Australian tender portals, so the block is global to the WebFetch tool rather than domain-specific. No tender detail page or specification document could be opened; EVERY recorded opportunity is therefore headline-level only (all counted in entries_pending_detail), with no deliverables/requirements/evaluation-criteria/documents extraction possible. Only WebSearch (routed through Anthropic infrastructure, not the egress proxy) was available; it is US-indexed and lags the live Australian portals, so most Tier 1 portal queries returned stale cached pages (open listings from mid-2026 already closed) or non-Australian noise (Tenders SA queries again surfaced South African SANRAL results). Within that limit this run confirmed three currently-open or recently-published buyer-originated opportunities and corrected one jurisdiction error in the raw snippets: (1) a Commonwealth AusTender ATM 'Provision of Ship's Boats to the Australian Border Force' (Dept of Home Affairs; the AusTender ATM/Show record and the Home Affairs Annual Procurement Plan both appear in results; status shown as 'Future'/open, closing 17 Nov 2026 per an aggregator snippet and still to be confirmed on the live notice); (2) a Tasmanian Dept of Justice prison amenities upgrade at Ron Barwick Minimum Security Prison (Risdon Prison Complex, Tasmania — the raw snippet mislabelled it as a generic state job; the facility location and the Tasmanian Treasury prequalification / $2M financial-limit language place it in TAS), closing 17 Nov 2026 per the aggregator snippet, unconfirmed on the Tasmanian portal; (3) the ACT Aquatic Strategy consultancy (Tenders ACT, closing 27 Oct 2026) — already first seen 2026-10-12, re-confirmed still open via Canberra Times coverage and carried forward under its existing dedup_key. Source discovery: three genuinely new buyer-originated sources identified with real URLs — Mount Isa Water Board (QLD statutory water GBE, advertises via QLD eTendering, has its own Current Tenders page), City of Cockburn (WA) e-procurement portal, and Shire of Derby/West Kimberley (WA) procurement/VendorPanel. Tier 3 (mandatory) was checked — SAP Ariba / SAP Business Network Discovery and the major-buyer portals expose opportunities only behind free supplier registration or invitation; no publicly-visible corporate RFx was confirmed and none were fabricated.
gaps: CRITICAL (ongoing since ~2026-10-05): WebFetch outbound egress is fully blocked by the environment's network policy. Every attempted fetch returned DNS failure (ENOTFOUND), including www.tenders.gov.au and example.com, confirming the block is global to the WebFetch tool, not domain-specific. No tender portal, detail page, or specification document could be retrieved this run.

Detail/deliverables/requirements/evaluation-criteria/documents extraction was impossible (detail pages and tender documents are only reachable via WebFetch, which is blocked). All 3 recorded tenders are headline-level only; deliverables/requirements/value/contact fields left null unless published in a search snippet or reputable news coverage.

All recorded closing dates and attributions come from WebSearch snippets (AusTender ATM/Show record, australiantenders.com.au aggregator listings, Canberra Times) and could NOT be confirmed against the live buyer notice. Treat each as provisional and reconfirm on the live portal.

Ship's Boats (ABF) closing date 17 Nov 2026 is from an aggregator snippet; the AusTender listing itself showed status 'Future' with no visible close date in the snippet. The AusTender ATM/Show record (2bb1025a-cc96-4552-d30f-496c61083d65) and the Home Affairs Annual Procurement Plan both appear in results, so the opportunity is real and buyer-originated, but the exact close date/ATM reference need confirmation on tenders.gov.au.

Ron Barwick (Tasmania) prison amenities upgrade could NOT be confirmed on tenders.tas.gov.au or any Dept of Justice page; detail is from a single aggregator snippet. The raw snippet did not clearly name the jurisdiction — TAS was inferred from the facility location (Risdon Prison Complex, Tasmania) and the Tasmanian Treasury prequalification / $2,000,000 financial-limit language. Tender ID, scope, and close date all require verification on the Tasmanian portal.

Tier 1 portals returned almost entirely stale cached results: NSW (tenders.nsw/buy.nsw) and WA (tenders.wa.gov.au) surfaced only mid-2026 listings already closed relative to 2026-10-14; QTenders/QLD results were old or aggregator-only; Tenders SA queries again returned South African SANRAL results (sa.gov.au did not index). SA, NSW and WA coverage this run is thin; deferred to a future run with WebFetch access.
NT QTOL returned only archived/test/awarded tender pages and portal help text; no current open NT tender could be confirmed. NT coverage deferred.
Universities: no open November-2026 university RFT could be confirmed (Adelaide, UniSQ, JCU snippets were stale or showed no current tenders). University coverage deferred.

Tier 3 private sector: SAP Ariba / SAP Business Network Discovery and the major-buyer portals (BHP, Rio Tinto, Woolworths, Coles, Qantas, EstimateOne construction network, etc.) expose opportunities only behind free supplier registration or invitation; no publicly-visible corporate RFx was confirmed and none were fabricated. Invitation-only consultancy RFPs remain out of scope by definition.
WebSearch is US-indexed and does not reliably reflect the live state of Australian tender portals, so even the recorded results and source discovery may lag the portals.
recommended_seed_additions: Whitelist the Tier 1 tender domains (tenders.gov.au, tenders.nsw.gov.au/buy.nsw.gov.au, tenders.vic.gov.au, qtenders.hpw.qld.gov.au/etender.hpw.qld.gov.au/supply.qld.gov.au, tenders.wa.gov.au, tenders.sa.gov.au, tenders.tas.gov.au, tendersonline.nt.gov.au, tenders.act.gov.au) and vendorpanel.com.au in the environment's network egress policy — without WebFetch access the routine cannot open, detail, or verify any tender.

Mount Isa Water Board — Procurement / Current Tenders (mountisawater.qld.gov.au/procurement): Queensland statutory water GBE; advertises via the QLD Government eTendering platform but maintains its own Current/Awarded Tenders pages.
City of Cockburn (WA) — Public Tenders / e-procurement portal (cockburn.wa.gov.au): buyer-originated WA local-government e-tendering channel.
Shire of Derby/West Kimberley (WA) — Procurement (sdwk.wa.gov.au), moving quotes and tenders to VendorPanel: buyer-originated WA remote local-government channel.

tenders.title: Provision of Ship's Boats to the Australian Border Force
tenders.buyer: Department of Home Affairs (Australian Border Force)
tenders.description: Commonwealth approach to market by the Department of Home Affairs / Australian Border Force for the provision of ship's boats (small marine craft) to the ABF. An aggregator snippet describes a Deed of Standing Offer with a single supplier, with an initial order of about 12 vessels and up to roughly 37 over the term; this scope could not be confirmed on the live AusTender notice.
tenders.reasoning: Discovered via WebSearch; the AusTender ATM/Show record (2bb1025a-cc96-4552-d30f-496c61083d65) and the Department of Home Affairs Annual Procurement Plan both appear in results, and an australiantenders.com.au aggregator listing (ID 614953) corroborates the title. Recorded against the buyer-originated AusTender source, not the aggregator.
tenders.notes: Headline-level only — WebFetch is blocked so the live AusTender notice and documents could not be opened. Closing date 2026-11-17 comes from an aggregator snippet and is unconfirmed; the AusTender snippet showed status 'Future' with no visible close date. Scope (standing offer, ~12 initial / ~37 total vessels) is from the aggregator and needs confirmation. Tender/ATM reference, value, contacts and documents all require verification on tenders.gov.au.

tenders.title: Ron Barwick Minimum Security Prison — amenities / shower upgrade
tenders.description: Facilities construction / amenities (shower) upgrade works at the Ron Barwick Minimum Security Prison, part of the Risdon Prison Complex in Tasmania. An aggregator snippet indicates the work is limited to contractors prequalified with the (Tasmanian) Department of Treasury and Finance up to a financial limit of $2,000,000.
tenders.eligibility: Contractors prequalified with the Department of Treasury and Finance (per aggregator snippet; unconfirmed)
mandatory_conditions: Prequalified with the Department of Treasury and Finance; financial limit $2,000,000 (per aggregator snippet; unconfirmed)
tenders.delivery_location: Risdon Prison Complex, Risdon Vale, Tasmania
tenders.reasoning: Surfaced as a WebSearch snippet (aggregator discovery signal) describing a prison shower-upgrade tender closing 17/11/2026. The raw snippet did not name the jurisdiction; mapped to Tasmania because Ron Barwick Minimum Security Prison is part of the Risdon Prison Complex in Tasmania and the Treasury-and-Finance prequalification / $2M financial-limit language matches the Tasmanian building-contractor prequalification scheme. Recorded against the buyer-originated Tenders Tasmania source.
tenders.notes: Headline-level only and UNCONFIRMED — WebFetch is blocked, so this could not be verified on tenders.tas.gov.au or any Department of Justice page. Jurisdiction (TAS) is inferred from the facility location and prequalification language. Tender ID, exact title, scope, value and close date all require confirmation on the Tasmanian portal. No deliverables fabricated.

tenders.title: ACT Aquatic Strategy Consultancy Services
tenders.description: ACT Government request for a consultant to develop a 10-year ACT Aquatic Strategy: set out the Territory's aquatic facility needs, the investment required and where it should go, including inspecting all government pools and estimating maintenance and upgrade costs (including electrification). Reporting indicates the strategy is expected to take about 12 months to develop with stakeholder consultation.
tenders.eligibility: Open; consultant with international and national experience in aquatic facility planning, design, construction, operation and regulation (per news coverage)
tenders.contract_term: Approx. 12 months to develop the strategy (per news coverage)
tenders.reasoning: Known opportunity (first seen 2026-10-12) re-confirmed this run as still open. WebSearch confirmed the 27 October 2026 closing via Canberra Times coverage of the ACT aquatic-strategy consultancy tender. Carried forward under its existing dedup_key so the aggregator de-duplicates it.
tenders.notes: Headline-level only — WebFetch is blocked so the live Tenders ACT notice and documents could not be opened. The description is drawn from news coverage (Canberra Times), not the tender notice itself; deliverables, value, contacts and documents require confirmation on tenders.act.gov.au.
